newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jerusalem tunnel closed while battles rage.
newsitem.headline: Jerusalem tunnel closed while battles rage.

text.p: Israeli officials closed the tourist tunnel in Jerusalem on Friday but that did not stop Israelis and Palestinians from fighting over it.
"Every Friday it is closed because on Friday and Saturday they are not working in Israel," insisted Hagai Elias, a spokesman for the Jerusalem municipality, when asked why it was closed.
Violence erupted after Israeli workmen on Tuesday made a second opening in the archaeological site beside Judaism's Temple Mount, site of Islam's third holiest shrine.

The act re-ignited Palestinian charges that Israel was trying to Judaise Arab East Jerusalem and triggered three days of clashes and gun battles in which more than 60 Palestinians and Israeli soldiers have been killed.
The United States and other Israeli allies urged right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to close the tunnel -- but he refused.
"There has been no order given to close the tunnel," Netanyahu's spokesman Michael Stoltz said on Friday.

Netanyahu's government came to power in June promising to bolster Israeli security, but the country's top soldier, army chief Lieutenant-General Amnon Shahak said on Friday that the army had only several hours notice of the opening of the tunnel.

For his part Israeli Police Chief Assaf Hefetz welcomed the closing of the tunnel on Friday, telling army radio: "The tunnel at the moment is closed. We think that the friction is unnecessary on a sensitive day like this."
